import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Geometry.SphereDiffusionGenerator
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Equiv

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Geometry.SphereAntipodalGenerator

open SphereDiffusionGenerator
open scoped Laplacian

/-- Negation transports the actual first derivative and commutes with the
existing extrinsic sphere expression. These are total-operator identities;
classical generator applications separately supply smooth tests and unit points. -/
theorem sphere_differential_operators_comp_neg
    {I : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
    (f : EuclideanSpace ℝ I → ℝ) (w : EuclideanSpace ℝ I) :
    (∀ h : EuclideanSpace ℝ I,
      fderiv ℝ (fun x => f (-x)) w h = -fderiv ℝ f (-w) h) ∧
    sphereLaplacian (fun x => f (-x)) w = sphereLaplacian f (-w) := by
  have hD (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ I) :
      fderiv ℝ (fun y => f (-y)) x = -fderiv ℝ f (-x) := by
    simpa only [neg_one_smul] using (fderiv_comp_smul (f := f) (x := x) (-1 : ℝ))
  have hDfun : fderiv ℝ (fun x => f (-x)) = fun x => -fderiv ℝ f (-x) :=
    funext hD
  have hH (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ I) :
      fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ (fun y => f (-y))) x = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) (-x) := by
    rw [hDfun]
    change fderiv ℝ (-(fun y => fderiv ℝ f (-y))) x = _
    rw [fderiv_neg]
    have ht := fderiv_comp_smul (f := fderiv ℝ f) (x := x) (-1 : ℝ)
    simpa only [neg_one_smul, neg_neg] using congrArg (fun L => -L) ht
  have hLap : (Δ (fun x => f (-x))) w = (Δ f) (-w) := by
    rw [InnerProductSpace.laplacian_eq_iteratedFDeriv_orthonormalBasis _
        (EuclideanSpace.basisFun I ℝ),
      InnerProductSpace.laplacian_eq_iteratedFDeriv_orthonormalBasis _
        (EuclideanSpace.basisFun I ℝ)]
    simp only [iteratedFDeriv_two_apply, Matrix.cons_val_zero, Matrix.cons_val_one, hH]
  constructor
  · intro h
    simpa only [neg_apply] using congrArg (fun L => L h) (hD w)
  · simp only [sphereLaplacian, hLap, hH, hD, neg_apply,
      map_neg, neg_neg]

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Geometry.SphereAntipodalGenerator

publication_context.statement: Let A(x)=-x on E=R^I, where I is finite. For every real-valued ambient function f and every w,h∈E, the first derivative of f∘A at w applied to h equals -Df(-w)[h]. The existing extrinsic spherical differential expression commutes with reflection: L_S(f∘A)(w)=L_Sf(-w). These equalities use the total Mathlib derivative operators. In the classical smooth setting at unit points, they give the familiar reflection symmetry of the spherical generator.
assumptions: I is a finite coordinate type with decidable equality, and E is the real Euclidean space with coordinates indexed by I.
f:E→R and w∈E are arbitrary; the first identity quantifies every direction h∈E. No smoothness, unit-norm or positive-dimension premise is imposed on the total-operator identity.
The radial correction uses max(|I|−1,0), implemented by natural-number subtraction before conversion to R.

steps.title: Transport the first derivative
steps.text: Negation is multiplication by the nonzero scalar -1. Mathlib transports the total derivative through this invertible change of variables, including the nondifferentiable cases handled by its total definition.
steps.lean:
have hD (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ I) :
      fderiv ℝ (fun y => f (-y)) x = -fderiv ℝ f (-x) := by
    simpa only [neg_one_smul] using (fderiv_comp_smul (f := f) (x := x) (-1 : ℝ))

steps.title: Differentiate the transported derivative
steps.text: The first derivative is the function x↦-Df(-x). Applying total derivative transport once more introduces a second minus sign; the two signs cancel. This gives equality of the actual continuous bilinear derivative expressions.
steps.lean:
have hDfun : fderiv ℝ (fun x => f (-x)) = fun x => -fderiv ℝ f (-x) :=
    funext hD
  have hH (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ I) :
      fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ (fun y => f (-y))) x = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) (-x) := by
    rw [hDfun]
    change fderiv ℝ (-(fun y => fderiv ℝ f (-y))) x = _
    rw [fderiv_neg]
    have ht := fderiv_comp_smul (f := fderiv ℝ f) (x := x) (-1 : ℝ)
    simpa only [neg_one_smul, neg_neg] using congrArg (fun L => -L) ht

steps.title: Contract and remove the radial terms
steps.text: The ambient Laplacian is the finite diagonal sum of the second derivative in an orthonormal basis, so its reflected value agrees. Bilinearity cancels the two signs in the radial Hessian. The sign of the first derivative is absorbed by replacing the radial vector w by -w. Substitute these three identities into the existing sphere expression.
steps.lean:
have hLap : (Δ (fun x => f (-x))) w = (Δ f) (-w) := by
    rw [InnerProductSpace.laplacian_eq_iteratedFDeriv_orthonormalBasis _
        (EuclideanSpace.basisFun I ℝ),
      InnerProductSpace.laplacian_eq_iteratedFDeriv_orthonormalBasis _
        (EuclideanSpace.basisFun I ℝ)]
    simp only [iteratedFDeriv_two_apply, Matrix.cons_val_zero, Matrix.cons_val_one, hH]
  constructor
  · intro h
    simpa only [neg_apply] using congrArg (fun L => L h) (hD w)
  · simp only [sphereLaplacian, hLap, hH, hD, neg_apply,
      map_neg, neg_neg]
